findings: legacy-attached-note-complete-height: The new painter truncates the total height correctly, but legacy ordinary-arrow allocation still uses fixed base3 plus half of all lines after the first. Unlike the self/Teoz branch, it does not compare complete arrow/note preferred heights. At note11/message13, line widths, line spacing and horizontal alignment match, but the canvas is190 versus188 and following event is2.3555 units too low; at note12 the accumulated difference is1.1777. These equal the first-line font-height differences omitted by that ordinary-note branch. Teoz text_precision_1 passes because it takes the complete-height branch. Causal next step: Use ArrowAndNoteBox's max of complete component heights and child centering for ordinary legacy attached notes as well; derive event advancement and paint from the same values.

style-consumption-is-partial: The corrected activationBox fallback is source-supported: lifeLine is a sibling, not a parent. Archived intermediate captures show all three reported losses, and fixed captures restore181818; fresh activationBox blue and root purple bars agree. However the CSS lifeLine red/orange is discarded by the lifeline painter, and root purple is lost by participant and arrow painters even though activation bars inherit it. Fresh sibling controls differ only on lifeline stroke. Root controls expose the same sparse-style-versus-legacy-skinparam split across primitives. This is an in-scope style/color dependency; the sibling correction is not whole style closure. Causal next step: Consume the resolved appropriate component signatures consistently for lifelines, arrows and participants, retaining sibling isolation and per-event style ownership. Do not restore lifeLine-to-activation fallback.

theme-self-note-allocation: Both known maker failures independently reproduce, and renamed multiline controls fail too. Legacy drops theme padding from self-arrow preferred width before Step1Abstract-equivalent note placement: cerulean Padding5 loses2*5 unscaled units (10.4167 in scaled SVG). Activation borders and glyph widths agree. Teoz shares that missing preferred width and also has a participant-origin translation and body-envelope discrepancy: known participant x is+5.2083 scaled, canvas width and height each-5.2083. Java composes the real head width, posC2+complete self width, note width and head/body/head envelope before wrapper insets. Rust reconstructs these independently through theme-specific participant padding, self width and raw_body_bottom. The exact required dependency paths are those functions, not a style-border fallback or a generic font waiver. The extra Teoz origin/envelope differences are not proven to have a single scalar cause. Causal next step: Unify the sequenceDiagramPadder-derived self-arrow preferred dimensions at all note/canvas consumers; separately port Teoz participant Real origins and head/body/head wrapper dimensions through the same component measurements. Preserve both failing pairs and require independently checked controls for all affected dimensions. No compensating offsets.

shadow-default-supported-inheritance-open: The scoped conversion correctly retains only ASCII digits/dots, with present malformed/default1.5. Six fresh controls cover zero/sign/unit, leading decimal, exponent text (1e2 becomes12), repeated dots, false and dot-only; all pass both engines across the matrix. Root numeric shadow4 combined with scoped nonnumeric default still fails complete output: note size and relative line metrics agree, but participant filter is absent and head/lifeline/canvas envelopes omit root shadow. Shadow conversion is supported locally; inherited/global product behavior is not accepted or waived. Causal next step: Keep ValueImpl conversion; route each component's inherited numeric shadow into its preferred dimensions and paint instead of relying on the sequence-wide boolean skinparam shadow switch.
